data.source_title: The effect of discharge destination and primary insurance provider on hospital discharge delays among patients with traumatic brain injury: a multicenter study of 1,543 patients
data.locator: Abstract, Methods/Results; Results, Discharge delays; Table 1. Delay defined as discharge at least 24h after case-management documentation of readiness.
data.source_setting: Four Level I trauma centers across three US states; adults with TBI and ISS >=9.
data.quantity: Median post-readiness discharge delay among delayed TBI patients
data.source_evidence_basis: Retrospective cohort measured discharge delay from case-management documentation that the patient was ready to actual discharge; median time from admission to delay start was 6 days, and median delay duration was 3 days.
data.limitations: Restricted to adult TBI patients at trauma centers and delay threshold >=24 h. Destination availability, insurance, and regional practices vary. The result is a conditional median among delayed cases, not a general all-patient distribution or RWJ measurement.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent clinical readiness and physical discharge as distinct states; allow downstream authorization, accepting-facility bed availability, and family coordination blockers. Use the median only as a conditional external stress-case benchmark.

data.source_title: The effect of discharge destination and primary insurance provider on hospital discharge delays among patients with traumatic brain injury: a multicenter study of 1,543 patients
data.locator: Abstract, Results; Results, Discharge delays and Table 1.
data.source_setting: Same four Level I trauma centers; delayed adults with TBI.
data.source_n: 210 delayed patients; reasons could overlap (percentages are not mutually exclusive).
data.source_evidence_basis: Medical-record review identified insurance processing/authorization, no accepting facility bed, and patient-related barriers such as language or family coordination as commonly reported delay reasons.
data.limitations: Reasons may co-occur; denominator is delayed TBI patients, not all admissions. Percentages should not be normalized to sum to 100 or treated as local rates. Not RWJ data.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as evidence that discharge planning needs parallel social-work/family, payer authorization, and post-acute placement transitions. Preserve overlapping blockers and external population scope; calibrate from local workflow data.
